items.description: Even after # CyberSecMonth comes to an end, stay alert 🚨! 🎃 Cybercriminals are not taking a break and might keep on tricking you! Here are some quick cyber tricks: 🍬Not every treat is sweet - beware of phishing emails and think before your click. 👻Don’t fall for a spooky ‘Boo!' - prevent your data from being leaked. 🪄Don’t fall for the spells - verify before you trust someone and share your personal information. items.title: *** Rule of law and privacy ***
items.description: *** Rule of law and privacy *** “Even though there is no single definition of the rule of law, there is a common understanding that the rule of law aims to guarantee protection of and respect for human rights.” With these words, @ Supervisor Wojciech Wiewiorowski, , opened his lecture on “Rule of Law and Privacy” at the ELSA Alumni Annual Meeting. In his speech, he highlighted the fundamental role of privacy in safeguarding individual dignity, freedom and autonomy, and explained why its protection is essential for a democratic state governed by the rule of law. The Supervisor emphasized: “In the digital age, protecting privacy is not merely one of the consequences of the rule of law. It is one of the conditions that makes the rule of law possible. Respect for privacy should therefore be regarded not only as a legal obligation, but also as an essential prerequisite for the functioning of a democratic society. # Privacy # RuleOfLaw # DataProtection # FundamentalRights

items.title: *** Data, Trust and AI in the Insurance Sector ***
items.description: *** Data, Trust and AI in the Insurance Sector *** Today, in the margins of the congress “The New Legal Framework for Insurance: Regulatory Challenges of Institutional Investment. Data and Agentic AI”, organised by Universidad Carlos III de Madrid, EDPS @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas took part in a roundtable on “Data, Knowledge and Transformation in the Insurance Sector”. The discussion addressed the role of data as a fundamental infrastructure for innovation and decision-making in the insurance sector, including data governance, data quality, interoperability and data analysis, as well as the associated legal, ethical and organisational challenges. In his intervention, Leonardo Cervera-Navas stated: “My thesis is simple: in insurance, data is not just an asset; they are a trusted infrastructure. And a trusted infrastructure is governed, not just used.” He also referred to the EDPS Opinion on the proposal on access to financial data highlighting that access to services necessary for daily life, such as credit, insurance or pensions, should not be made conditional on excessive data processing.
